chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Adhinah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: Walking is muhaththah.

key_terms.الْمَشْيُ: Walking (the act of moving on foot)
key_terms.مُحَدَّثٌ: Created / Temporal / Event (something that has a beginning and is not eternal)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that walking is 'muhdatha' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses the term 'muhaththah' (created/temporal) to describe 'al-mashy' (walking), illustrating that divine actions are events occurring in time rather than eternal attributes co-existing with God's essence. This distinction is pivotal in Shia kalām for refuting the Mu'tazila and Ash'ari views on the nature of God's will and power, affirming that while God is eternal, His actions are created and temporal. The hadith thus serves as a concise epistemological tool to differentiate between the necessary existence of the Creator and the contingent nature of His deeds.
